title: DNS: Validate labels for ASCII encoding
description:
While RFC 1035 considers label components to be opaque
octet arrays and does not formally require any specific encoding
ASCII is "strongly recommended" and "assumed".

get_dns_names() returns domain names as opaque byte strings and expects
clients to validate the output, which not all do, and is a bit
wasteful, since none care about other encodings that aren't ASCII.

This changes it to accept only ASCII. Bytes outside ASCII are replaced
with U+FFFD (unicode replacement character).

Fixes #18484.

notes.body:
Note that Microsoft LDAP officially uses RFC 1035 encoding with compression pointer support, but their documents say that the strings are UTF-8.

I don't know how true that is, or how often UTF-8 is actually used, but as dissect_mscldap_string() calls this, it would technically break anything using non ASCII.
Thanks, I will be more conservative for now and fix the callers instead.
